text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends Wood, Animal Park Set We have almost the entire Thomas and friends Fisher-Price wood set of the new type of connectors, and we do not have any of the old style tracks from any brands. Overall the new tracks stay together very well and are easy to put together, but in all honesty my three-year-old sometimes has to bring these new style wood tracks to me to get them apart, which she never has to do with the tiny set of traditional tracks that grandma has at her house. What is nice is that you can attach the tracks from either direction, since both sides connect identically.

We have the busy island set, the farm set, cranky at the docks, the train station, and the huge Tidwell sheds station. All of these sets fit together beautifully and provide a lot of different play options for the kids. However, the main complaint I have had is that most of these sets have not come with enough tracks. Even the huge sets, come with just enough tracks to barely get it together if you are very careful and mindful with how you put things together.

The main advantage of a set like this animal park one, is that you get a whole lot of tracks and every piece in it can be used to connect all of the big and exciting things in those huge sets. My daughter also really loved the simplicity of this set, that she doesn't really have to think too hard about how it goes together, she can just wind and turn and connect things up without too much planning ahead.

Overall this set adds to the larger Thomas sets really nicely and is a great way of introducing a little more interest and a lot more tracks into the busy island set or another one of the bigger sets.
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends Wood, Animal Park Set

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars Solo: A Star Wars Story Kessel Run Millennium Falcon 75212 Building Kit and Starship Model Set, Popular Building Toy and Gift for Kids (1414 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This LEGO STAR WARS KESSEL RUN MILLENIUM FALCON BUILDING KIT (75212; 1414 pieces) is a great set—definitely one of my all-time favorites. When completed, the kit produces a large, heavy but solid, fun-to-play-with model of the “Kessel Run” Millennium Falcon that’s featured in the new Han Solo movie (“Solo: A Star Wars Story”, released on 5/24/2018). As an adult, I really love this Millennium Falcon, which has a large removable space shuttle in front that accommodates a minifigure, and two powerful, spring-loaded bolt shooters. The bolts always fly 18” or more (you get four bolts). There is also a gunnery pod for minifigures in the center circular area.

The build is fairly demanding, which makes it a lot of fun for experienced builders. The parts you assemble aren’t always symmetrical, and there are a lot of left- and right-handed components, so you have to pay attention to the instructions as you build. There are some “studs not on top” segments, and some components (like the removable transparent nose cone) that are attached “sideways” to vertical studs. There are also a few items (e.g., the lever-action doors at the top front) that attach with Technic parts.

Most of the “triangular” pieces on the top of the model swing up for easy access to the furnished interior. Inside there are chairs that accommodate minifigures, control panels (done with stickers), coffee bars, and engine parts storage boxes. The stickers aren’t excessive, and are easy to position. (I use a thin, flat, metal spudger to pick up and place the stickers accurately.)

The set has several specialized bricks that I haven’t seen before (e.g., the bricks that form a channel for the space shuttle to slide in and out of the front of the model). It also has some unusual building techniques that are used to link together pieces that are installed along a curved line. The model has four sturdy feet, which allow it to stand on a flat surface with space for the underbody gun turret.

The set has only 1414 pieces, but many pieces are very large (e.g., the triangles that open on top). The finished model is a big, substantial toy (the circle is 12” across).
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Solo: A Star Wars Story Kessel Run Millennium Falcon 75212 Building Kit and Starship Model Set, Popular Building Toy and Gift for Kids (1414 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

32" Play Kitchen, 2 in 1 Toy Kitchen & Grill Playset Kitchen Pretend Play Toys Kitchen Playset Kids Kitchen Set with Cooking Accessories Pros: The kids love the kitchen playset, so much so that my 4.5-year-old niece preferred it to playing her favorite computer game for a full week and the 2-year-old couldn't be tempted away even by birthday cake. It's still the first toy she heads for when she visits. One kid can play on each side, so they can play at the same time. They didn't seem bothered that things didn't work quite right. I also like that they have whole food cooking ingredients (fruit, veggies, meat, eggs) rather than a bunch of finished foods or deserts.

Cons: The kitchen is basically held together by the parts having been firmly pressed into place. Thus, even lifting it by the roof can cause parts to come off. We've moved the kitchen around several times with no problem as long as you use the handles on the purple side panels. The oven and cupboard doors were initially hard to open, but luckily use has loosened this up some. The sink faucet pulls out during play, one of the BBQ-stick holders comes off very easily (when removing the stick to put food on or off), and some of the stickers don't want to stay on. Replacing the batteries is going to be a pain as they're on the underside of the cooking surface. The plastic food is a soft plastic, so the egg got crushed when stepped on. And cooking sure is noisy! I wish there was a way to lower the volume. So the adults feel like this isn't as good a product as it could be (3 stars) but the kids give it 5 stars.

ORIGINAL: This kitchen and grill playset is the perfect height for my two-year-old niece to play with. She likes to pretend like she is cooking, so she enjoys playing with the set. There is some assembly required, and the instructions are simply line drawings. Keep the box since looking at the two sides in the pictures is of more help in assembly than the instructions. Keep in mind that you will not fully tighten the joints until done with the first couple steps. The barbecue sign is a thin sheet of cardboard, so I assume that the thicker board is supposed to be put in the slot along with it. I don't know why they didn't just print the sign on the thicker board or even just past it on. As it is, you're trying to fit two separate sheets into a slot seemingly meant only for the thicker one. I had someone try to help me get it into the slot, but it was too tight to get in very far. I ended up cutting off some of the top just to make it fit (though it turns out I didn't need to do this. It could have just stuck up without running into anything). Except for this, assembly was not particularly difficult.

You use three AA batteries to power the sound. Once you hook up the spigot, you can put water in the sink and then pump it out through the spigot. The plastic food was recognizable as specific types of food, and the pots, plates, utensils, and bottles are distinct and fairly sturdy. Since it is merely pressure that fastens the joints together, this could come apart under especially hard play, but it's unlikely a two-year-old will cause any problems with it. Overall, I'm pleased and my niece is extremely happy to play with it when visiting my house.

UPDATE: The stickers are coming off after about a week, and not just because of use. They just didn't stick well to the water bottle and utensils. The handles on the cupboard about the oven is difficult to open because there's nothing to really get a grip on the handle. It's the perfect height for a 2-year-old, but my 4.5-year-old niece has to kneel to use it. (We wanted something small since we don't have lots of room to store the toys, but this maybe isn't something that will span a large age range.)
text_fidelity_b: 32" Play Kitchen, 2 in 1 Toy Kitchen & Grill Playset Kitchen Pretend Play Toys Kitchen Playset Kids Kitchen Set with Cooking Accessories

text_fidelity_a: WE Games 4 Player Shut The Box Dice Board Game with Lid- Walnut Stained Wood - Large Coffee Table Size - 14 Inches, for Family and Adult Game Night Play in Classroom, Home or Bar Product listing says 12 yrs and up. Don't listen to it. If you have kids as young as 4 and starting to learn adding and subtracting, this game will be super educational! My youngest is 5 and she bugs us every day to play this game. Kids under 12 will love this game, trust me. It's not just adding and subtracting, for more advance play, you can do multiplication, division, any math you can think of. Lets say your roll a 4 and a 3, but you're out of tiles to make 7. But you have a 9 and a 3 in play, well if multiplication is part of the game then 4x3 is 12, hence, you can shut the 9 and 3 tiles. Lets say you roll a 5 and a 4, but you have no more tiles that add up to 9, but you have a 3 in play. What's the square root of 9? It's 3, now you can shut that 3. Any math you can think of is fair game, that's how we play it. Play this game with your kids, and they will learn math faster! 5-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: WE Games 4 Player Shut The Box Dice Board Game with Lid- Walnut Stained Wood - Large Coffee Table Size - 14 Inches, for Family and Adult Game Night Play in Classroom, Home or Bar

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll I have been around Barbie dolls my entire life. My mom collected them and my sister got into it. My daughter has had a few here and there, but none of them was the quality that this doll is. I did not expect it to be fantastic quality, but it even fell short of my lower expectations.

WHAT IS THE DOLL LIKE?
The doll comes in a clear plastic package which is not overly attractive, in fact it looks stark and not like the usual Barbie stuff. The doll itself is packaged with two pieces of plastic sticking out from inside her head. It is then attached to the board in the back so you have to cut those pieces to get it off of the backing. That means you have to be careful of the hair. Once you managed to do this, you have to stick the plastic ends back into the skull of the doll to keep the sharp ends from pricking your child or you.

The outfit is kind of cute and the colors are attractive. The doll itself is a rigid plastic doll- not the bendable twist and turn type that they have had in the past. The head piece has a knob type attachment which makes it able to move in almost any direction. The problem is in this case, the head is so easy to move it is borderline bobble head.

HOW DOES THE HAIR COLOR WORK?
The hair color looked like it would be a lot of fun! It has a plastic piece that is similar to a flat iron in shape. Inside the *flat iron* piece are a group of colored waxy blocks. The idea is that you comb the doll's hair and separate it into strands. You press the flat iron type piece over the hair, squeeze it shut as you draw the hair through and it leaves the color on the hair.

The hair is waxy in feel, probably to make the color work better than traditional Barbie hair. In this case, however, it does not seem to do much for the process. The hair colors are not too great. They come off as crumbly and waxy and very spotty on the hair. If you run your fingers over it, you will get some on your fingers. This will stain so if your child plays with this near anything white or light colored, it could stain it.

The color blocks are almost like you mix waxy crayons with silicone to make it a bit softer. The result is uneven kind of unimpressive color on the hair. It is not overly bright and does not look like the pictures promised.

THE BOTTOM LINE
My daughter was not impressed by this doll. The body is very rigid, making for a boring play toy. The hair is very uneven and has a waxy feel to it. The colors come out crumbly and uneven, and color blocks probably will only last for a day or two of constant play and then run out. The colors will stain some things so if you plan to let your child run free with this, you may regret it if you have anything white you don't want stained. The head is so easily moved that it is unpleasant to play with and use. The outfit is cute and colorful and the shoes are not too bad either.

My daughter kept saying that she expected more substantial color that was like a watercolor marker or something instead of a crumbly waxy substance that barely sticks to the hair in a few random spots. She kept taking out her other Barbie dolls and saying how much more she liked those. I give this two stars because it has a nice outfit, and if you want a disposable toy for your child, it will serve the purpose. If you want a sturdy toy they will play with over and over, I am thinking this might not be it for you.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll

I chose to review it because I have a third grade cousin on whom I could test the set, and it was a hit in every way. The experiments are well designed, and the instructions are easy to follow--something I think is extremely important. I also love how easy it is to clean up after you are finished--everything washes up easily. You will need a few extra items for some of the experiments, but most homes will have these things around--things such as baking soda and vinegar. This set claims to produce 50 experiments, but some of these are variations on one another, so I would say 25 is closer to the truth. Still, that is a lot for the price.

As a retired teacher, I appreciate well-designed toys that offer learning experiences as well as play, and this toy does not disappoint. It is perfect for those long days of summer when your child is bored. Parents will need to be involved, especially for younger children, but to me that is a plus. For the price, this toy cannot be beat. And it may give your child an idea or two for the school science fair! Highly recommended.

Unsolved Case Files: Cold Case Murder Mystery Game: Who Murdered Harmony Ashcroft? | Can You Solve The Crime? The only reason this isn't a 5-star review is the racist casting in the mystery that had nothing to do with the story.

A friend gave this to me knowing my love for true crime. I've always wanted to try the Hunt a Killer boxes, but was always put off by the price.

No spoiler review:
- The case file includes newspaper clippings, evidence files, interview transcripts, photos, and more. Your first puzzle is to prove the innocence of Bones, the only non-white person in the game who was a homeless drunk that was wrongfully accused and jailed for the crime. (Obviously, racism is very much a problem with our justice system in real life. However, depicting that in a fictional puzzle game? We'll never solve this problem if we continue to portray that happening. Furthermore, there was NO STORY REASON WHATSOEVER for it.)
- You select your answers to the puzzles on their website, and if you're right you can open the first seal additional evidence envelope. I was worried the answer selection would spoil the real answers, but we didn't have to worry about that at all.
- We ended up becoming so invested in the case, after a couple hours in we decided to sleep on it and solve the first puzzle the following day. We couldn't stop talking about it.
- Once you play it once, you can't play it again. However, you don't have to mark any of the evidence so you can easily just put everything back in the envelope and give it to a friend. For the price as well, that's a lot better than most true crime puzzle games that are WAY more expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Unsolved Case Files: Cold Case Murder Mystery Game: Who Murdered Harmony Ashcroft? | Can You Solve The Crime?

I can see him putting it in his pocket and bending it and couldn’t stand the thought. He promised to take it home and not bring it back. I told him I know he would want to show his friends the card and now that he’s not allowed to bring it to school they may not believe him so I told him if anybody questioned him to come see me and I can let them know I seen it in person. Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a toy made with greenness in mind. It is manufactured with recycled materials and is great for environmentally- conscious parents who wants their kids to have some creative fun while also minimizing environmental impact. Designed for children between the ages of three and six, it is one of the few building toys that doesn't involve blocks or other interlocking rectangular pieces.

This toy involves building arrangements of flowers on a green, branch like base and there is no end to the different number of creative arrangements that kids can make. The pieces consist of leaves and three different flowers and they can be stacked and arranged in any number of ways. The combinations are endless and every time my girls play, it turns into a new adventure. My girls love creative toys, flowers, and art, so a toy like this is very likeable and enjoyable to them.

I like that this toy is made using recycled materials and I like the small, cube- shaped box included for storage. Most manufacturers do not even think about including a small storage box, and this often forces parents to use plastic bags or plastic containers to store the pieces. With an included box, there is no need to reach for these environmentally- unfriendly storage receptacles that may one day wind up in a landfill. Instead, you just use the included box, which is also made from recycled material, and the pieces will be safe to use for the next adventure.

With its lack of batteries, green composition, and creative encouragement, this toy is certainly a nice change from most others, but does it have any possible flaws or potential issues? I can think of only a few. One is the small pieces. They can easily become misplaced, so parents need to watch closely to make sure that kids place all of the pieces back into the box. Of course, the nice fact here is that you can afford to lose a few because, since they are all interchangeable, it won't prevent the toy from being used again and again. Another issue is that this toy could become boring after a while. There are those youngsters who crave action, lights, and sounds in their toys and if yours is one of them, then they may grow tired of the toy in a short time.

Recycling is certainly a good idea and creative toys that require imagination and not so much of the lights and sounds so common with kids' toys today are definitely a nice change of pace. Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a very nice little toy from Green Toys and it makes a great choice for these reasons. The possible building combinations are endless and while some kids may tire of it in a short time, it still has enough positive qualities and creative entertainment value to make it worth a purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games

Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.
10/10 will buy from again.

text_fidelity_a:
Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer) This is a very complex and detailed game. It's not for children and it requires that the people playing are ready to spend several hours dealing with the complexities of the system.

At the same time, its a fun game. There are no dice which would be used to randomize events. The game is affected by your play and that of your opponents.

Overall, this is a resource allocation game. You start with two "meeples", who are effectively workers on you farm. Each turn you can send them out to collect resources or to perform special actions that build additional space or activate a special card. After certain turns you have to "feed" your meeples giving up some resources you had previously collected. In the end points are scored based on how big of a home and farm you have grown over the course of the game. The game winner is the one who manages to plan ahead and use his meeples wisely.

Of course, the challenge is to collect the resources at the right times. Most stocks grow if no one collects them that turn, so there is a bit of tactically plotting. Do you send someone to collect the small amount of wood this turn, or do you let it go and hope no one claims it. All of the resources play out this way, you have to decide which is going to be the most value at that time.

If you can find people willing to put the time in, this Is an excellent game.
text_fidelity_b: Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer)

It weighs 1 pound 8.9 ounces (706 grams). It measures 5 1/5 inches across (14cm), 3 1/2 inches (9cm) deep and 4 inches (10cm) at it's height. The sculpting is sturdy. It consists of two solid resin pieces that are attached with 2 very sturdy hinges. The hinges are sturdy enough to support the heft of the lid while it is displayed completely open. It does not tip, nor attempt to close once opened completely. The front features a clasp that has a loop for a lock. All hardware pieces are sturdy, and attached to the Mimic with small screws. I will attempt to edit the review to let you all know the results upon arrival of the lock.

The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box is styled and sculpted to be true to Mimic D&D monster lore. The interior bottom really does resemble the obnoxious monster, instead of simply being a storage box. I count this as a plus, as nearly anyone can simply paint a plain trinket box and call it a Mimic. I am especially impressed with the interior sculpting, it's terrifying, especially the sculpted eye inside and 21 teeth inside the top lid. The interior bottom of the Mimic has 25 teeth and sculpted gross Mimic guts. Scary stuff for sure! The exterior painting is quite nice. It does not scratch away easily. I'm happy with the company's paint job, but with it being resin, it could be removed and repainted by anyone wishing to do their own customization or paint job. Conjurer Co. By Merhoff & Larkin is proudly stamped into the resin of the bottom exterior. Each box will have some slight variations, as this is clearly a hand-crafted, hand-painted piece. Personally, I'm a fan of handmade items, and find this box as a very pleasant surprise.

I found The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box has exceeded my expectations. I did my own comparison with many other artistic interpretations of a Mimic along with alternative storage boxes. This does the job of easily storing 3 sets of common sized acrylic dice along with serving as a horrifying prop during play. I'm excited to bring The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box to the table, it's an impressive hand-crafted prop. Between games, it will make a nice display piece with some other D&D props and figures on a shelf. It's a good value, especially once I made some comparisons between The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box, other dice storage boxes and different types of hand-crafted Mimic props.

The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box is an ideal, unique gift for any table-top role play enthusiast, figure collector or your beloved local Dungeon Master. It would also serve as a nice gift for yourself. It comes packaged in a small, white cardboard box with an interior lined with 1/2 inch Styrofoam. It would be easy to wrap in paper to present as a gift.

As this is a 3-in-1 set, there are instruction books for two other builds, a saber-toothed tiger and a scorpion. I might like the tiger best of all, just because he looks a little derpy.

Overall, I like the 3-in-1 sets, since I think they show kids a different range of techniques, and how bricks can be repurposed from one build to another.

CVCBSER Smooth Swing Dueling Lightsaber, Increase Motion Control 12 Sets Sound Effect Light Saber, with 16 Colors Changeable Premium Metal Handle Lightsabers for Adults and Boys Gift (Silver) [[VIDEOID:acf24d91cee31c0de845571b6cd24d7b]] This is a very nice light saber. Good heft to it with lots of features. There will be a learning curve, but hopefully my tips as well as the video demo will make it easier for you. Remember that it is all in the blinking:

After assembling and charging your saber, you start off in SLEEP mode, meaning NOTHING should be illuminated. Hold the power button until the power ring illuminates and you hear a voice saying POWER ON. Now this is called OFF/AWAKE mode. Off meaning the lights/effects are not turned on yet, but the power button ring is illuminated. More on this OFF/AWAKE state later. But here, you simply tap the button to turn on the lights and effects. Now you are in ON/AWAKE mode, and here are the commands for ON/AWAKE mode:

ON/AWAKE MODE COMMANDS:
-------------------------------------
ONE BLINK: Hold the button until it BLINKS one time, then release. LOCK-UP effect is now enabled. It basically sounds like your saber just hit some electrical wires and is going crazy. Tap the button to get out of it.

TWO BLINKS: Hold the button until it BLINKS twice, then release. The saber will cycle through the color choices. Once you like a color, tap to set your color choice.

THREE BLINKS: Hold the button until it BLINKS three times, then release. You will hear a quote from the movies. To hear a different quote, hold until it BLINKS three times again, then release. Basically keep holding and releasing after three blinks to cycle through the quotes.

FOUR BLINKS: This turns OFF the lights/effects. But, the power ring is still illuminated, which means you are back to OFF/AWAKE mode, and here are the commands for OFF/AWAKE mode:

OFF/AWAKE MODE COMMANDS:
--------------------------------------
ONE BLINK: This allows you to set the sound volume. You can set between NO SOUND, LOUD SOUND, and SOFT SOUND.

TWO BLINKS: This is for light effects. You can have it STABLE, UNSTABLE, or PULSE. Stable gives a consistent solid light, which is what I have on during my demo because it's easier to capture on video.

THREE BLINKS: This is for setting a theme music. You can cycle through 5 songs, and the 6th is no music. So if you leave it at any one of the songs, whenever to turn on the lights/effects, music will be on too. So if you don't want any music, make sure you cycle all the way to no music.

FOUR BLINKS: You can cycle through more movie quotes, one of which is, "The force is with you Luke..."

LASTLY, to put it sleep. Hold the button for 10 seconds, so when you do this. It will go through its blinking, but just disregard them until the red illumination is completely off. This takes about 10 seconds. You are now in SLEEP mode. The same mode as when you first assembled and charged the saber. To play again, hold the power button until it illuminates, and you are back to OFF/AWAKE mode.
text_fidelity_b: CVCBSER Smooth Swing Dueling Lightsaber, Increase Motion Control 12 Sets Sound Effect Light Saber, with 16 Colors Changeable Premium Metal Handle Lightsabers for Adults and Boys Gift (Silver)

People didn't like getting eliminated and didn't like someone needing to moderate/narrate the game. The resistance is best played with more people. The more the merrier definitely is true here. Some people will play as the resistance and some as spies. The spies are trying to sabotage the missions while the resistance is trying to complete the missions. The game has a mission leader who will pick which players are going to go on the mission. The game then opens discussion to all players to decide if that is the best choice of players for the mission.

Overall, We enjoyed the game, but when playing with only 5 players, it's a bit too easy and people don't really get into the discussion. When playing with 8-10 players, the game is a lot more fun as people really get into the accusations and deciding who should go on the different missions. 3Doodler Start Emoji & Symbols Doodleblock Kit with 2 Pack of Refill Filaments (3D Pen Not Included) First things first: There are two different popular 3Doodler pens: 3Doodler Start and 3Doodler Create. Each uses different filaments and they are NOT interchangeable. The two 3Doodler pen models use different melting temperatures: Start is cooler; Create is hot. This pack is for the 3Doodler START -- it will NOT work with 3Doodler Create! Be sure you know which 3Doodler you have.

That said -- this is a nice addition to the 3Doodler Start collection. I've been using my 3Doodler to create embellishments for paper crafts -- primarily hand-crafted greeting cards and a little scrapbooking. The emojis and symbols in this set work well in terms of size -- perfect for my cards. I use the heart and star most often, as well as the asterisk, pound sign, and ampersand. There are two packs of filaments: blue, red, green, gray and white, mint/aqua, yellow and orange. Good colors that work with a variety of color schemes.

Overall, a good refill set with the addition of the emoji/symbol DoodleBlocks. I like it!

text_fidelity_a:
Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset Littlest Pet Shop Fairy Fun Roller Coaster Set is a girl's toy featuring the Littlest Pet Shop characters. It is a colorful, cute toy that offers action without the need to purchase batteries. The operation is mechanical so kids can play as long as they want without the worry of batteries dying out.

This toy is nice for many reasons and besides the lack of batteries, the toy offers some simple operation and continuous action. All your girl has to do is press the lever, which moves the stairs upward and slowly transfers the small figures and their vehicles to the top of the slide where they glide around and wind up back at the base of the stairs. If you continue to press the lever, it will gradually pick up the next Littlest Pet Shop figure and send it up the stairs to the top of the slide where it will, once again, make its way around the slide to the base of the stairs.

My girls like this toy and both they and I find it to our liking. If I had to find some type of fault, it would be the tendency for the small vehicles to sometimes get out of place when they reach the base of the stairs. I haven't witnessed any problems with the vehicles gliding smoothly down the slide- the only problem I notice is that the little vehicles will sometimes get out of place at the stairs, requiring some manual assistance to re- position them. This is most likely to happen if kids get carried away and move the lever too quickly. Keep the speed at a moderate to slow rate, and there shouldn't be any problem.

Mechanical toys are nice and even though the Fairly Fun Roller Coaster Set has little or no educational value, it is still a nice toy for girls in the target age group. It is cute, colorful, and provides hours of simple amusement without the need to purchase batteries.
text_fidelity_b: Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset

Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 50 cars is too much at once.

Days as a five year old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 50 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 50 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels Basic Car 50-Pack."

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ We absolutely love our dinosaurs, dragons, and lifelike statues of real animals from this brand, and this extra-large dinosaur is no exception. The thing you should know about these is that they are a very hard resin like material. This makes them much better for children who are old enough to use the statues responsibly and not bash them on things such as their little sister, because they are very hard and heavy and have absolutely no give to them. On this particular model, the end of the tail is the most dangerous part aside from the sheer size and weight of the overall piece.

This dinosaur is much larger than the cheapo dinosaurs that you get in multi-packs that are made in China, and the level of craftsmanship and detail here is sufficient for even the most exacting dinosaur connoisseur. That said, though the description talks about scoop shaped teeth being a major part of what makes this dinosaur cool, I was unable to really discern much scoop detail on the teeth, given the relative size of the teeth versus the relative size of the dinosaur. Just something to be aware of. But that's not me complaining about the level of detail.

I love the artistic detailing on the hide, the bluish bumps on the back, the little spines, and the huge amount of expression in the face. My toddler son is just beginning a dinosaur phase and enjoyed stomping this large dinosaur through his truck collection and roaring with great feeling. I think that as his knowledge of dinosaurs expands, so will his appreciation of all the small differentiating details that give this dinosaur personality, character, and most importantly, accuracy.

As long as you are aware of the hard and heavy resin material used to create these, you will be deeply impressed by the detailing, durability, and potential for imaginative play inherent in the figure.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Oil Pastels Portfolio Series, Water Soluble, Colors may vary, 12 Count (52-3612) I tried the Crayola neon pastels first and then decided to get a bigger set so I bought the portfolio crayolas set and have included a picture of all 24 colors.
They are bright with a variety of colors including black and white. Crayola has never come across as a high-end brand, but in oil pastels they are highly regarded as some of the best, and I agree. If you watch some of the videos on YouTube about how to use oil pastels you will realize how great these are. You can also see comparison videos, and the crayola brand gets very high marks. Oil pastels don't make a mess unless you use your finger to blend them, and then your finger will be a big mess. But you can clean it with baby wipes or soap and water or lotion to get down into your skin if it's dry. You can use traditional rolled paper sticks for blending also. These come packaged neatly so you can keep them in their original slots in that packaging. Besides coloring with them you can also use a wet brush to blend them, and you can layer them on top of each other or blend them together with your finger. I have also seen them covered with a clear acrylic paint and then used again on top of that paint. You can see that on YouTube. These are an inexpensive way to enjoy yourself artistically and produce beautiful results just like painting when you add the water or vodka or a blender like turpenoid.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Oil Pastels Portfolio Series, Water Soluble, Colors may vary, 12 Count (52-3612)
